transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, to be honest... what really scared me enough to make this appointment is that I’ve started having these thoughts lately. Just things like, it would be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. 

I want to be clear that I don't have any actual plan to harm myself or anything like that. But... just noticing my mind going there was enough to make me realize I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have you ever experienced a period like this in the past where you felt this low?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had sad days or tough weeks over the years, just like anyone else. But... no, I've never experienced a period quite this low before. This is really the first time my mind has ever gone to a place like that.
Did these feelings start around the time of a specific life change or a stressful event?
Yes, actually. This has been going on for about eight months now. It started right around the time my brother's health... and his behavior, really... just changed so suddenly.
Beyond these thoughts about not wanting to wake up, have you been feeling a persistent sense of sadness or a loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. Most days it just feels as if... well, like a gray film has settled over everything. Even when I’m just going about my normal routine, making a cup of tea or looking out at my garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me. I try to reason my way out of it, but I just can’t seem to shake it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns since this all began?

My appetite hasn't really changed much, to be honest. But my sleep... yes, that has been quite difficult. 

At night, I just fall asleep rather unevenly. And then, almost without fail, I wake up around three or four in the morning. My mind just starts going over everything—thinking about phone calls I need to make, all the paperwork and forms, worrying about whether I handled things correctly with my brother the day before. I just lie there awake with it all. By the time morning actually comes, I feel as if I’ve hardly rested at all.
Have you noticed that you have been struggling with a significant lack of energy or feeling physically slowed down for most of the day, nearly every day, since this started?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired because I'm not sleeping well, but I wouldn't say I feel physically slowed down or completely out of energy. I still get up and do what needs to be done around the house. It's more just the sadness and the worry that are exhausting, rather than my body feeling slow.
Beyond the worry about your brother, have you found yourself feeling a sense of worthlessness or experiencing excessive, inappropriate guilt about things you've done or failed to do?

Yes, I do. I just... I keep going back over my brother’s decline in my head. I keep telling myself that if I had been a better sister, or just more attentive to him, I would have noticed something was wrong sooner. It's hard not to feel like I could have prevented some of this if I had just been paying closer attention.

Since this began eight months ago, have there been any periods of a few weeks or longer where you felt like your normal self again, or has this feeling of sadness been present almost every single day?

No, there really haven't been any weeks where I felt like my old self. It's been present almost every single day. Most days, I feel as if a gray film has just settled over everything. Even when I’m doing simple things, like making a cup of tea or looking out at my garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me. I just can’t quite reason my way out of it, no matter how I try.
During those times when you are lying awake at night or thinking about your brother, do you feel physically restless, like you need to pace or move around because you cannot sit still?

No, not really. I don't get the urge to pace around or anything like that. When I'm lying awake at night, I mostly just... I just lie there. My mind might be going over and over things about my brother, but my body stays pretty still. I don't feel that physical need to get up and move.
